chapters.summary: Holmes is hard at work on a new case when Watson visits him at Baker Street. A masked visitor arrives, who turns out to be the King of Bohemia. He wants back a photograph that shows him with Irene Adler, a woman he once wrote letters to. Holmes agrees to help. He and Watson go to Briony Lodge, where Holmes stages a fake fire to find where the photograph is hidden. Irene escapes with her husband, leaving only a note. Holmes gets the photograph anyway, but Irene has outwitted him.

chapters.summary: Dr. Watson visits Sherlock Holmes and meets Jabez Wilson, a pawnbroker with bright red hair. Wilson tells how his assistant Vincent Spaulding showed him an advertisement offering paid work to red-headed men. Wilson applied, was hired by Duncan Ross, and spent eight weeks copying the Encyclopaedia Britannica. One morning he found the office closed and a notice saying the League was dissolved. Holmes noticed signs that Spaulding was secretly digging a tunnel from the cellar. That night Holmes, Watson, the police agent Jones, and bank director Merryweather wait in a bank cellar. They catch John Clay, who was trying to rob the gold, and his accomplice escapes.

chapters.summary: Sherlock Holmes and Dr. Watson talk about strange real-life cases. Miss Mary Sutherland visits Holmes because her fiance, Hosmer Angel, vanished on their wedding morning at a church. She has a small income and a stepfather, Mr. Windibank. Holmes studies her clues, including her typewritten letters from Angel. He writes to Windibank asking him to visit. When Windibank arrives, Holmes shows that the letters were typed on Windibank's own typewriter and that Windibank was Angel in disguise. Holmes locks the door and explains the plot. Windibank runs away. Holmes says the law cannot touch him.

chapters.summary: Watson travels with Sherlock Holmes to the west of England to look into the death of Charles McCarthy at Boscombe Pool. McCarthy's son James has been arrested for the killing. Holmes and Watson meet Lestrade and Alice Turner, who insists James is innocent. At the pool, Holmes reads the ground and finds clues, including a stone and cigar ash. He works out that the killer was left-handed, lame, and had been in Australia. John Turner then confesses to Holmes and Watson that he killed McCarthy to protect his daughter. James is later acquitted.

chapters.summary: Watson is visited on a stormy night in September by John Openshaw, a young man from Horsham. Openshaw tells how his uncle Elias received a letter with five orange pips and the letters K. K. K., and died in what was called a suicide. Years later his father received the same warning and died in a fall into a chalk-pit. Now John has received the warning too. Holmes advises him to put a page from his uncle's diary into the brass box and place it on the sundial. Holmes explains the secret society of the Ku Klux Klan. The next morning Watson reads that Openshaw was found drowned near Waterloo Bridge. Holmes sends a warning to the captain of the Lone Star, but the ship is later lost at sea.

chapters.summary: Dr. Watson is called at night by Kate Whitney, whose husband Isa has vanished into an opium den. Watson goes to the den and finds Isa, then sees Sherlock Holmes disguised as an old opium smoker. Holmes explains that Neville St. Clair disappeared after his wife saw him at a window above the den. Holmes takes Watson to The Cedars in Lee, where Mrs. St. Clair shows a letter from her husband. Holmes then goes to Bow Street, where he washes the beggar Hugh Boone's face and reveals him to be Neville St. Clair. St. Clair explains he had disguised himself as a beggar to earn money and hid his secret from his family.

chapters.summary: Dr. Watson visits Sherlock Holmes the day after Christmas and finds him studying an old battered hat. Holmes explains that a commissionaire named Peterson found the hat and a goose after a man lost them in a fight. Holmes reasons out details about the hat's owner, Henry Baker. Then Peterson returns with a blue stone found inside the goose's crop. Holmes learns the stone is the stolen blue carbuncle, and he places an advertisement to find Baker. Baker comes to claim the hat and takes a new goose. Holmes and Watson then trace the geese to a salesman and a small man named James Ryder. Ryder confesses that he hid the stone in a goose to smuggle it out. Holmes lets him go and says he hopes to save a soul.

chapters.summary: Helen Stoner visits Sherlock Holmes and Dr. Watson early one morning. She tells them her twin sister Julia died after hearing a whistle at night and crying out about a speckled band. Helen now fears the same fate, since she sleeps in Julia's room. Holmes and Watson travel to Stoke Moran and examine the rooms. Dr. Grimesby Roylott, Helen's stepfather, arrives in town and threatens Holmes. That night, Holmes and Watson wait in Helen's room in the dark. They hear a hiss and a strange sound, and then a terrible cry. They find Dr. Roylott dead, with a swamp adder wrapped around his head. Holmes puts the snake in the safe.

chapters.summary: Dr. Watson is woken early by a guard who brings in Victor Hatherley, a young hydraulic engineer with a bloody, injured hand. Hatherley tells how Colonel Lysander Stark hired him for a night job at Eyford, claiming a hydraulic press was needed for fuller's-earth. At the house he met a frightened woman who warned him to leave. Stark trapped him in the press, which began to crush him, but he escaped through a panel and jumped from a window, losing his thumb. Holmes and Watson then travel to Eyford, where they find the house burning and a severed thumb in an upper window.

chapters.summary: Sherlock Holmes receives a letter from Lord St. Simon, whose bride vanished at their wedding breakfast. Holmes reads newspaper clippings with Watson, then questions the nobleman about his bride, Hatty Doran. Lord St. Simon describes the dropped bouquet, a note-like gesture, and the maid Alice, and says Flora Millar, a former dancer, caused a disturbance. Lestrade arrives soaked from dragging the Serpentine, carrying the wedding dress and a card-case note signed F. H. M. Holmes sees the hotel bill on the back and says the bride is a myth. Later Holmes produces the missing bride, Mrs. Hay Moulton, and her first husband, Frank Hay Moulton, who was thought dead. Lord St. Simon storms out, and Holmes explains his reasoning.

chapters.summary: Alexander Holder, a rich banker, rushes to Baker Street in distress. He tells Holmes that the Beryl Coronet, which he kept in his house, was damaged, and that his son Arthur was caught holding it. Holmes and Watson visit Fairbank, where Holmes studies the house and the snowy tracks. He finds that Mary Holder, the banker's niece, had passed the coronet to Sir George Burnwell through a window. Holmes disguises himself, gets the missing gems back, and the banker apologises to Arthur. Mary has run off with Sir George.

chapters.summary: Violet Hunter, a governess, visits Sherlock Holmes about a strange job offer. Mr. Jephro Rucastle wants her to cut her hair and wear a blue dress, and pays very well. Holmes sends her to the Copper Beeches in Hampshire. There she finds a locked wing, a hidden prisoner, and a huge mastiff. Holmes and Watson go to the house and find the prisoner gone, and Rucastle is badly hurt by his own dog. Mrs. Toller explains that Rucastle had locked up his daughter Alice to stop her marrying Mr. Fowler.

synopsis: Sherlock Holmes and Dr. Watson solve a series of strange cases in London and the English countryside. A king wants back a photograph of himself with Irene Adler, but she outwits Holmes and escapes with her husband, leaving only a note. A red-haired pawnbroker's assistant is revealed as a criminal digging a tunnel into a bank, and John Clay is caught in the cellar. Mary Sutherland's missing fiance turns out to be her stepfather in disguise, and he runs away. At Boscombe Pool, James McCarthy is cleared when John Turner confesses to killing his father to protect his daughter. John Openshaw is threatened by a secret society and later found drowned. A missing man is found begging in disguise, a stolen blue carbuncle is traced through a goose, and Dr. Roylott dies from a swamp adder. Victor Hatherley escapes a deadly press, Lord St. Simon's bride is revealed alive, and Holmes recovers the Beryl Coronet. At Copper Beeches, Violet Hunter finds a hidden prisoner, Alice Rucastle, locked away by her father.
majorArcs: Holmes outwitted by a clever woman
